rationale: PINS the CommonJS form of the child_process signal. The taint sink rule's evidence that a bare `exec` is Node's own shell — rather than the project's own function of the same name — was read only off an `import_statement` or an `import ... = require(...)` clause. `const { execFileSync } = require("child_process")` is the same fact in a different spelling, and the signal scan had no case for a CALL, so the evidence never arrived and the sink was never recorded. This is a false NEGATIVE, and the more costly direction: no sink means no flow can be traced into that call, so `bb_security` cannot report a real command injection there at all. Measured before the fix over the tracked corpus: 24 files, 27 missing sink records, 0 records wrongly present, 0 lost — every missing record a bare exec-family call in a file that genuinely requires child_process. The exclusion is pinned separately in `taint-sink-require-not-loader`, because the signals are per-FILE and a negative cannot be observed in a file that also has a real require.

expectTaintSinks.note: TRUE POSITIVE, and the reason the defect mattered: a bare execFileSync whose only evidence is this file's `require("child_process")`. Pre-fix this symbol carried no taintSinks at all, so no user input reaching `root` could ever be reported as command injection here.
